subject: Post-call recap: PayLane inference economics, batching & cache pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@paylane.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: PayLane inference economics, batching & cache pilot

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we have alignment before we scope the pilot.

High-level pain points you called out
- High per-request cost and unpredictable token spikes during peak processing windows.
- 95th percentile latency that occasionally breaches the 500ms SLO for your customer-facing scoring endpoint.
- Internal ops overhead for model version rollouts and quantization testing.

Goals you shared
- Bring inference cost down within a $8k–$12k/mo budget for the payments fraud scoring pipeline (starting target window across production traffic).
- Maintain 95th p50 latency < 350–400ms for the low-latency scoring path.
- Run a short pilot to prove cost and latency levers before committing to reserved capacity.

Cost/TCO levers we discussed
- Batching: moving from 1-request immediate execution to 20–50 request micro-batches during steady periods. Expected raw token-cost delta: 20–35% improvement depending on concurrency and request size.
- Prefix/KV caching: cache common request prefixes and intermediate KV states for repeated user flows. Conservative hit-rate assumption: 10–20% initially; with prompt sanitization we can aim for 30–40% within 2–3 weeks. That multiplies savings on top of batching.
- Quantization & model variant routing: use a quantized 4-bit variant for non-critical scoring and fall back to fp16 for edge cases. Estimated additional 15–25% cost reduction vs baseline fp16.
- Intelligent routing: route low-priority batchable traffic to cheaper variant/region while reserving hot path capacity for low-latency requests.

Pilot scenarios (attached spreadsheet shows line-level math)
- Minimal pilot (baseline): 5M tokens/mo, single-zone hosted usage, expected monthly cost range: ~$9k–$14k depending on current qps distribution.
- Optimized pilot (batching + cache): same workload with batching (avg batch=30) + conservative cache (15% hit) + quantized routing -> expected monthly cost range: ~$5.5k–$8.2k and p95 latency projected to improve ~20% on scoring endpoint.
- Aggressive optimization: 10M tokens/mo full caching rollout + reserve capacity -> projected cost ~$7k–$9k but with stronger latency SLAs and lower variance.

ROI framing
- Payback window for investing in a pilot and engineering support: often within 2–3 months once cache and batching stabilizes for mid-size workloads due to token-unit savings and reduced GPU hours.

Recommended next steps
1) Confirm you want to run the Optimized pilot (4 weeks) vs Minimal pilot. We recommend Optimized to show measurable savings.
2) If agreed, Lauren will provide a short pilot runbook and SE checklist (access, sample prompts, latency SLOs).
3) We provide an access-only trial environment with monitoring dashboards and a small reserved buffer for bursts.
4) PayLane to share representative prompt set and 1 week of anonymized production traces for accurate sizing.

Attachments: paylane-20260715-tco-scenarios.xlsx (cost scenarios and sensitivity)

Open questions we left on the call
- Is the $8k–$12k/mo target firm or flexible for the first 2 months of pilot?
- Any compliance gating beyond SOC 2 Type II that would block a hosted proof-of-concept?
- Do you want Redwood to model both 5M and 10M token scenarios with different cache hit curves?

Thanks — happy to sync with the broader infra team if useful.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@paylane.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: PayLane Architecture Team <infra@paylane.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: PayLane inference economics, batching & cache pilot

Karthik, thanks for the thorough summary. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Budget: the team is targeting closer to $12k/mo as a hard upper bound for the pilot period. We can stretch to $14k once we see solid savings, but the procurement owner will push back on anything above $14k without a clear ROI.
- Burst capacity: we need to retain a cushion for peak fraud-burst windows (we see short spikes ~3x baseline QPS for 8–12 mins). Can you detail how Redwood handles short bursts without violating latency targets?
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required; we also need documentation on data retention controls and an option for dedicated VPC if the pilot looks headed for production.

We can provision sample prompt traces — I will ask infra to anonymize and send 3 days of traces. For the pilot, we prefer a 2-week ramp to validate controls quickly and then extend to 4 weeks if results look good.

If you can send the pilot runbook and a conservative cost model that keeps us within $12k/mo baseline, we can try to get procurement pre-approval.

Best,
Elena Morales
Director of Engineering, PayLane

Lauren/Monica — quick internal note following Elena's reply. Procurement wants to keep pilot spend <= $12k/mo initially and is asking for SOC2 + data retention notes. Elena is asking about burst handling; they see 3x QPS spikes for short windows.

Ask for Lauren: can you prepare a 1-page pilot runbook + conservative cost model that keeps expected spend under $12k for a 2-week ramp and shows headroom for 3x bursts without SLA breach (ideally by using our reserved buffer and short-term autoscale policy)? Also include what we need from PayLane (sample traces, API keys, expected concurrency).

Monica: loop in CS for a quick procurement intro, and be prepared to provide pricing language for a 4-week optimized pilot if procurement signs off.

Thanks — Karthik
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@paylane.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runbook & burst strategy for PayLane (attached)

Hi all — attaching a short pilot runbook (pilot-runbook-paylane.md) and calling out the technical and economic bits up front. TL;DR: we can hit PayLane's $12k/mo target during a conservative 2-week ramp with these constraints and still provide a 3x burst buffer.

Technical plan
- Pilot duration: 2-week ramp + optional 2-week extension.
- Regions: run initial pilot in us-west to minimize network RTT; can mirror to us-east for redundancy later.
- Batch sizing: continuous micro-batching, target avg batch=25 for scoring traffic. For low-latency hot path, we keep batch=1 with prefetched KV cache lookup.
- Cache expectations: initial hit rate assumption 15% (sheet contains sensitivity to 10/15/30%). With basic prompt normalization we expect to reach ~30% within 10 business days.
- Burst handling: reserve a small hot pool (dedicated capacity fraction) sized to absorb 3x baseline QPS for 10 minutes. For longer bursts, autoscale policy will spin additional units; billing during autoscale uses on-demand pricing but we throttle to avoid uncontrolled spend.

Economic summary
- Conservative 2-week ramp: projected cost ~$5.8k (prorated), stays within the $12k/mo constraint.
- Full 4-week optimized pilot: projected cost range $6.5k–$8.3k depending on cache adoption; shows 25–35% token cost reduction vs baseline.
- Notes: these numbers assume sample traces provided by PayLane match production distribution. If your production is 2x the supplied traces, we will re-run sizing with updated numbers.

Required from PayLane to start
- 3 days of anonymized prompt/trace data (preferably representative of peak and off-peak).
- A test API key with a staging endpoint or sample payload format.
- Authorized contact for procurement and security review.

I attached the pilot-runbook-paylane.md and the cost scenarios spreadsheet. Happy to jump on a quick 30-min technical sync tomorrow to walk infra through the runbook.

Lauren Bishop
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
